questions.question_text: What are the zeroes and the $y$-intercept of $f(x) = (x - 2)(x + 6)$?

options.why: Read the zeroes straight off the brackets as $-2$ and $6$ instead of solving each factor for zero.
Multiplied the bracket numbers as $2 \times 6 = 12$, dropping the signs of $f(0) = (-2)(6)$.
Read the zeroes straight off the brackets and also multiplied $2 \times 6 = 12$ without the signs.

questions.solution_text:
Zeroes occur when $f(x) = 0$:
$(x - 2)(x + 6) = 0$
$x = 2$ or $x = -6$
$y$-intercept is $f(0)$:
$f(0) = (0 - 2)(0 + 6) = -12$
Zeroes: $x = 2, -6$; $y$-intercept: $-12$

questions.question_text: Find the zeroes and the $y$-intercept of $f(x) = x^2 - 7x + 10$.

options.why: Factorised as $(x + 2)(x + 5)$ instead of $(x - 2)(x - 5)$, so the zeroes came out negative.
Carried the minus sign of the $-7x$ term onto the constant, writing $f(0) = -10$.
Factorised as $(x + 2)(x + 5)$ and also carried the minus sign of $-7x$ onto the constant for $f(0)$.

questions.question_text: Find the zeroes and the $y$-intercept of $f(x) = (x + 5)(x - 3)$.

options.why: Read the bracket constants as the zeroes instead of solving $x + 5 = 0$ and $x - 3 = 0$.
Dropped the negative sign when multiplying $5$ by $-3$ to find $f(0)$.
Swapped the output $f(0) = -15$ with the two inputs where $f(x) = 0$.

questions.solution_text:
Zeroes occur when $f(x) = 0$:
$(x + 5)(x - 3) = 0$
$x = -5$ or $x = 3$
$y$-intercept is $f(0)$:
$f(0) = (0 + 5)(0 - 3) = -15$
Zeroes: $x = -5, 3$; $y$-intercept: $-15$

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between zeroes and intercepts for a function $y = f(x)$?

options.text: A zero is an $x$-value where $f(x) = 0$, representing an $x$-intercept; $f(0)$ is the $y$-intercept when $0$ is in the domain.
A zero is the value of $f(0)$, which represents the $y$-intercept on the graph.
options.why: Confused the definition of a zero with the $y$-intercept evaluation $f(0)$.

options.text: A function can have at most one zero, but can have infinitely many $y$-intercepts.
options.why: Reversed the uniqueness property of functions for inputs versus outputs.

options.text: The zeroes of $f(x)$ are the coordinates $(0, y)$ where the graph crosses the $y$-axis.
options.why: Gave the $y$-intercept coordinates instead of the $x$-intercepts.

questions.solution_text:
A zero of $f(x)$ is an input value $x$ satisfying $f(x) = 0$, which is an $x$-intercept on $y = f(x)$.
The $y$-intercept is the output value $f(0)$ when $0$ is in the domain. Otherwise there is no $y$-intercept and $f(0)$ is undefined.

questions.question_text: Find the zero and the $y$-intercept of the linear function $g(x) = 4x + 12$.

options.why: Solved $4x + 12 = 0$ as $4x = 12$, forgetting to change the sign when moving $12$ across.
Gave the coefficient of $x$ as the $y$-intercept instead of evaluating $g(0) = 12$.
Solved $4x = 12$ without changing the sign and also read the coefficient $4$ as the $y$-intercept.

questions.question_text: For the function $f(x) = -3(x - 1)(x + 4)$, what are the zeroes and the $y$-intercept?

options.why: Forgot to multiply by the leading coefficient $-3$ when finding $f(0)$.
Reversed the signs of the roots from the brackets.
Treated the constant multiple $-3$ as producing an extra zero at $x = -3$.

questions.question_text: Find the zeroes and the $y$-intercept of $f(x) = x^2 + 3x - 54$.

options.why: Read the constants in $(x + 9)(x - 6)$ as the zeroes instead of solving each factor for zero.
Used the coefficient of $x$ as the $y$-intercept instead of evaluating $f(0)$.
Dropped the negative sign of the constant term when evaluating $f(0)$.
